title: Deterministic combat target selection with explicit formation coordinates
objective: Implement deterministic single/all/row/column target selection while keeping PAL3 ElementPosition-to-row/column mapping outside the domain until that mapping is supported by runtime/data evidence.
hypothesis: An explicit formation-coordinate adapter contract can support all current TargetRangeType selection semantics without guessing how the upstream elemental positions map to rows and columns.
claim_boundary: This experiment selects targets only. It does not apply damage/healing to multiple targets, prove the real PAL3 ElementPosition row/column layout, or add Unity presentation behavior.
source_evidence: Pinned upstream TargetRangeType defines FirstPartySingle/All, EnemyPartySingle/All, EnemyPartyOneRow and EnemyPartyOneColumn.
Pinned upstream ElementPosition defines six ally and six enemy element/center slots.
No pinned-upstream resolver or explicit row/column mapping was found, so the domain requires explicit row/column input rather than infer it.

attempts.description: Resolve living first/enemy party targets deterministically; require explicit anchor for single/row/column; filter defeated actors; validate unique target keys and formation coordinates; expose read-only results.
attempts.fix: Pre-CI contract review added global target-key uniqueness after identifying that all-target selection could otherwise return a duplicate actor key from different coordinates.

verified_invariants: Single-target selection requires one living anchor on the required party.
Party-all selection excludes defeated actors and uses deterministic row/column ordering.
Enemy-row and enemy-column selection use explicit adapter coordinates rather than infer ElementPosition geometry.
Duplicate target keys are rejected globally.
Duplicate formation coordinates are rejected within a party.
Returned target collections are read-only wrappers rather than raw arrays.
reusable_lessons: Do not collapse semantic target range names into guessed geometry when upstream exposes the range enum but not the coordinate mapping.
Target identity uniqueness is a separate invariant from formation-coordinate uniqueness.
Keep target selection pure before adding multi-target state mutation.
next_recommended_experiment: Step 5B applies one already-supported damage effect to the selected target set, spends MP once per cast, and emits one resolved Damage fact per affected target.
